title: streaming-lifecycle-controls: client cancel / disconnect handling + reconnect/resume + server timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Motivation: Production streaming connections have several observed failure modes: clients sending explicit cancel signals, abrupt TCP disconnects, intermittent reconnects that should resume in-progress streams, and long-tail server-side stalls/timeouts that cause partial outputs to be lost. This PR implements a unified lifecycle control surface to make the streaming behavior predictable and interoperable with OpenAI-compatible clients.

Summary of changes: 1) wire protocol: introduce connection-level lifecycle events ("connection:cancel", "connection:disconnect", "connection:resume") and a resume token for resumable streams; 2) server behavior: deterministic server timeouts with configurable grace periods and automatic buffered flush on timeout; 3) client cancel handling: cancel requests now produce an immediate "cancel_ack" control event and triggers KV cache cleanup per request-id; 4) reconnect/resume: short-lived resume tokens allow reconnecting clients to pick up partial state (token TTL default 60s, configurable); 5) OpenAI compatibility layer: map OpenAI-style client-cancel semantics to our lifecycle events and expose resume semantics via the compatibility headers; 6) structured output and tool/function calling: ensure tool-call sequences are preserved across reconnects and cancellations, and structured JSON chunks include sequence indices to allow idempotent reassembly by clients; 7) telemetry and tracing: add lifecycle phase tags to traces and metrics for SLO reasoning.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-8247) - [x] Unit tests for lifecycle state machine - [x] Integration tests for reconnect/resume and server timeout behavior - [x] Backwards-compatible OpenAI mapping layer tests - [x] Docs and SDK snippets updated - [x] Perf regression run (no significant regressions)

Why this change: Customers have reported flaky streaming behavior when networks drop or when they use client-side cancellation for user interactions. These changes make behavior explicit, reduce resource leaks, and provide a migration path for OpenAI-compatible clients wanting to resume sessions.

Notes: Resume tokens are intentionally short-lived to limit state leakage; long-lived persistence should be handled via our dedicated session APIs if needed. The default behavior preserves prior semantics unless users opt-in to resume mode via the streaming.resume=true header.

Links: Design: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8247/streaming-lifecycle-controls; Incident reference: SUP-4021.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial lifecycle state machine + protocol (aisha), integrate resume token store and eviction policy (ravi), tests + openai compatibility mappings + docs (miguel)
review_comments: Miguel Santos: small nits on naming in lifecycle.go; suggested 'CancelAck' instead of 'CancelConfirmed' — addressed in commit 2.
Jane Li: please add a test for a reconnect after server timeout; added integration test streaming_reconnect_timeout in commit 3.
Ravi Kumar: discussed TTL tradeoffs for resume token in review thread; settled on 60s default and made TTL configurable via STREAM_RESUME_TTL env var.
QA (Lina Park): observed intermittent e2e failure on Windows runner; flake traced to socket linger on Ctrl-C, added additional cleanup in streaming_handler.go and re-ran CI.
release_notes: Add streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel ack, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume with short-lived tokens, and deterministic server timeout behavior. Backwards compatible with OpenAI-style clients via compatibility headers. See docs/api/streaming_lifecycle.md for migration notes.
post_merge_actions: bump sdk/python minor to include streaming.resume header mapping
announce in #platform-api and include migration blurb
schedule canary rollout: 25% first 24h, monitor lifecycle error metric
